help.description: Frequently asked questions, definitions and tips for operators
help.faqQ1: What should I check at the start of my shift?
help.faqA1: Open the Dashboard before you start operating and check for offline workstations or pending alerts, so you catch problems before they get reported to you.
help.faqQ2: A workstation shows as "Offline", what should I do?
help.faqA2: Check the device's network connection and that the service is running. Check the last activity report time in the Workstations section.
help.faqQ3: How do I know if a workstation is printing through the cloud or in contingency?
help.faqA3: In Workstations, check the workstation's badge: if it says "Contingency", print traffic is going straight to the printer. If it doesn't show that, it's printing normally through Lexmark CPM (the cloud).
help.faqQ4: What does it mean for a workstation to be "in contingency"?
help.faqA4: It means printing is redirected straight to the printer, bypassing the cloud (Lexmark CPM). It turns on by itself when the cloud fails, or an admin forces it manually.
help.faqQ5: When should I turn on forced contingency for a workstation?
help.faqA5: When the workstation can't print through the cloud (CPM is down or unstable) and you need it to keep printing anyway. Turn it on with the shield button in Workstations; it can be done per workstation, per VLAN, or for the whole organization.
help.faqQ6: I turned on contingency for a VLAN but users still can't print, why?
help.faqA6: The VLAN probably has no printer assigned. Contingency needs at least one active device in the workstation's VLAN to be able to receive the print job.
help.faqQ7: How do I turn off contingency once the cloud is working again?
help.faqA7: From the same shield button you used to turn it on (Workstation, VLAN, or Organization), turn it off so the workstation goes back to printing through Lexmark CPM.
help.faqQ8: A device stopped printing, where do I start?
help.faqA8: First check its status in Devices; if that looks fine, check the VLAN it belongs to and whether the workstation is in contingency. Most "not printing" cases come down to one of those three.
help.faqQ9: Why does an IP appear in "Pending IPs"?
help.faqA9: A new device connected to the network and has not been authorized yet. Review it in that section and approve or reject it.
help.faqQ10: Can I approve any pending IP I see?
help.faqA10: Don't approve it blindly. Before authorizing it, confirm with the IT team that the device is legitimate — that way you avoid granting access to something that shouldn't be on the network.
help.faqQ11: I don't see a device on the network map.
help.faqA11: Confirm that the VLAN is correctly assigned and that the device's IP is within the configured range.
help.faqQ12: I forgot my password, what should I do?
help.faqA12: Use the "Forgot your password?" option on the login screen to receive instructions by email.
help.faqQ13: A technical issue keeps recurring, should I escalate it right away?
help.faqA13: Before escalating, check the Knowledge Base — it might already be documented with a known fix. If you find nothing there, then escalate.
help.glossaryDef1: The account that groups users, workstations, VLANs and devices under one client or site.
help.glossaryDef2: A person with system access; their role (Admin or Operator) determines which sections and actions they can use.
help.glossaryDef3: Virtual local network that segments network traffic to group workstations and devices.
help.glossaryDef4: A connected workstation or device that the system monitors and manages.
help.glossaryDef5: The client application installed on each workstation (a system tray icon) that runs remote actions and reports its status.
help.glossaryDef6: Mode in which the workstation prints directly to the printer, bypassing the cloud (Lexmark CPM). It turns on when the cloud fails or when an admin forces it manually.
help.glossaryDef7: The cloud service that manages printing in normal mode. It's the "normal" printing path, as opposed to contingency.
help.glossaryDef8: A printer or other network equipment associated with a workstation or VLAN.
help.glossaryDef9: An IP address detected on the network that has not yet been authorized by an administrator.
help.glossaryDef10: Notation for expressing a range of IP addresses (e.g. 192.168.1.0/24). Used to define which IPs belong to a VLAN.
help.glossaryDef11: Run an action (restart Tray, update, etc.) on multiple workstations at once, by VLAN or organization.
help.glossaryDef12: Backend health dashboard (database, queues, containers) for administrators.
help.glossaryDef13: Status and performance data that each workstation periodically sends to the system.
help.glossaryDef14: Geographic view of workstations based on their location.
help.glossaryDef15: Diagnostics for the network connection between workstations and the central system.
help.glossaryDef16: Feature that lets you view a workstation's screen remotely.
help.glossaryDef17: Historical log of actions performed in the system: who did what and when.
help.glossaryDef18: Notifications or announcements sent to workstations or operators from the system.
help.glossaryDef19: Mechanism that distributes new Tray versions to workstations without manual intervention.
help.glossaryDef20: Technical articles used as context for AI-assisted debugging analysis.
help.glossaryDef21: Reference guides and manuals for the system.
help.glossaryDef22: Global, per-VLAN, or per-workstation settings that define system behavior.
help.glossaryDef23: A copy of the system's database and files kept for recovery purposes.
help.glossaryDef24: Certificate that encrypts communication between workstations and the central server.
help.glossaryDef25: Bulk import of workstations or devices from a file to keep the inventory up to date.
help.glossaryDef26: Chronological activity history for a specific user.
help.glossaryDef27: A text file where a workstation records its activity and errors. Downloaded or analyzed to diagnose why something didn't work.
help.glossaryDef28: AI-assisted diagnostics of a workstation's logs to find the root cause of an issue.
